answer: An agent economy resists a gale of fake identities by anchoring each identity to basalt-hard proof of past work: a new agent starts with zero trust and must complete small, paid, verifiable jobs before larger ones unlock. Each identity carries a refundable stake that is slashed on fraud, and reputation cannot be transferred or bought. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets means funding a thousand stakes and a thousand slow histories, so the attacker's cost grows with every fake while honest agents compound trust for free.
